title: Repertoire
intro: Build your personal opening plan move by move. Save what you want to play and the replies you expect from your opponents.

whatIs.title: What is a repertoire?
whatIs.body: It is your own map for the opening: your moves, the opponent replies you want to prepare for, and your notes for each position.
whatIs.reassurance: You do not need to prepare everything at once. Learn an opening with NexoChess, import one, or build it yourself.

learn.title: Learn an opening without swallowing the whole tree
learn.intro: Choose an opening or defence. NexoChess splits it into progressive lines: understand the sequence first, practise it next, then review it when it is due.
learn.methodUnderstand: Know which line you are studying and always keep the context.
learn.methodFollow: Walk through the variation move by move on the board.
learn.methodPractice: Rebuild your moves from memory with your coach.
learn.methodReview: Spaced repetition brings difficult lines back sooner.
learn.methodAdd: Add only the lines you actually want to play to your personal repertoire.
learn.searchLabel: Search opening, defence, variation or ECO
learn.familyIntro: Start with the first lines. Deeper variations appear later so you are not overwhelmed.
learn.depthHelp: Lines are ordered progressively. You do not need to learn them all: add the ones that fit your game to your repertoire.
learn.prepareAs: I want to learn it as
learn.practiceInstruction: Play your moves. The opponent will reply with the line you are training.
learn.startPosition: Start from the initial position and watch how the opening is built.
learn.keepItHelp: Add it to your personal repertoire. It will merge with existing lines without deleting variations.

coach.welcome: Choose an opening and I will teach it in small pieces. You do not need to memorise a hundred variations today.
coach.family: We will work through {{opening}} from shallow to deep. Start near the top and only go deeper when the earlier lines feel comfortable.
coach.lineStart: First look through the whole line and understand the sequence. Then I will ask you to rebuild it without seeing it.
coach.practiceStart: Your turn now. I will play the opponent moves and you answer with what you just prepared.
coach.opponent: This is the opponent's reply in the variation. Keep the context before choosing your next move.
coach.correct: Good. That is the continuation you are training. Keep following the idea of the line.
coach.tryAgain: That is not the prepared move in this line. Read the position and try again; ask for a hint if you need one.
coach.hint: The hint shows the prepared move. I will count it as help so this position comes back sooner in review.
coach.move: Watch how this move changes the position. Do not memorise only the square: notice which piece improves and what changes in the centre.
coach.completed: Line completed. I will schedule it to return when reviewing is useful, sooner if you needed help.

explanations.start: Look at the starting position and the full sequence first. The goal is to recognise how this variation reaches its characteristic structure.
explanations.castle: Castling prioritises king safety and usually connects the rooks. Notice when the opening makes it possible.
explanations.check: This move gives check and forces an immediate reply; forcing moves are useful landmarks for remembering a line.
explanations.capture: A tension is resolved with a capture. Notice which pawns, files or diagonals open after the exchange.
explanations.knight: The knight develops or relocates. Check which central squares it controls and which pieces it frees.
explanations.bishop: The bishop enters the game along a diagonal. Notice which pawn move released it and what target appears.
explanations.queen: The queen enters the position. Remember its concrete purpose so you are not memorising a queen move without context.
explanations.centrePawn: A pawn occupies or challenges the centre. These moves often define space and the pawn structure of the opening.
explanations.pawn: This pawn move changes squares permanently. Notice the space it gains, the piece it frees, or the break it prepares.
explanations.piece: The piece improves its placement within the line's plan. Connect the move with development, pressure or coordination.

review.title: Review exactly what is due
review.intro: Lines you have practised return at growing intervals. Mistakes and hints bring them back sooner; solid lines stop bothering you every day.
review.emptyBody: Practise a line in Learn and NexoChess will start scheduling its reviews.
review.next: Your next review is scheduled for {{date}}.
review.queueHelp: Start with the first one or choose a specific line. You will always see which variation you are training.

transfer.title: Import games or your own repertoire
transfer.intro: Turn PGN games or repertoire files into editable NexoChess branches. NexoChess backups also preserve notes and base positions.
transfer.pgnHelp: Accepts one game, multiple games, or a repertoire PGN with variations and comments.
